approach: ADDITIVE ONLY (self-clears, suite stays @frozen): no frozen operator.feature scenario is narrowed or rewritten. New use-case group 'The seat's identity — calling in to the bunker' + its scenarios. Verify with classify-edit-class before the gate; no Clearance floor expected.

MODEL: Operator is a singleton at the bunker. cyberlegion already carries both objects — the bunker is `standing-operator` (kind standing: never exits, session-independent, durable mailbox), the desk is AgentRecord.presence bound by `unit claim <handle>` keyed on the ROLE HANDLE (last claim wins; an exited occupant reads as an empty desk). The operator node names neither.

OWNER DECISIONS (in-session): (1) claim is UNCONDITIONAL on seating — register as itself, then `unit claim operator`; fail-soft when no multiplexer. (2) A missing standing owner FAILS LOUD and routes to init-cyberlegion — Operator never mints durable hub identity (init-cyberlegion's explicit-yes boundary). (3) Operator DRAINS the bunker mailbox on seating and leads with what is waiting.

EVIDENCE (.research/operator-skill-grill/conclusion.md, findings A+B): standing-operator holds 36 messages, 36 unread, 0 ever acked, 2026-07-14 to 2026-08-11. `unit claim operator --show` and `unit claim homa --show` both report `presence: none` — nobody has ever called in, which is why every standing-owner doorbell falls back to the hub main pane (a pane dead since 2026-07-13).

REJECTED FIX (recorded so it is not re-proposed): `unit register --handle operator` on seating. It does NOT change routing (preferStanding picks the standing record regardless), it keys continuity on the PANE (resolveSelfId reads the pane index and register honors that id — in a recycled pane it takes over whatever unit died there; the incident pane held an exited POD), and it adds an Nth live holder to a handle that already has two. The verb is `claim`, not `register`.

OUT OF SCOPE (follow-ups): preferStanding falling through to matches[0] for two live non-standing units sharing a handle (packages/cyberlegion identity.ts — different project spec); the stale hub `attach` binding; the 36-message operational backlog.

why: operator.feature: 12 additive scenarios across two new use-case groups — 'The seat's identity — calling in to the bunker' (register this session under its OWN handle before claiming; never register as `operator`; claim unconditionally, taking the desk even when another session holds it; fail-soft when no multiplexer; fail-loud + route to init-cyberlegion + never mint when the standing owner is absent) and 'The bunker mailbox — reading what it took' (drain `mail inbox --owner operator --unread` on seating and lead with it; ack an acted-on report, leave an unacted one unread; a spawn brief names the seat's handle, never a session id) — plus two scenarios appended to the EXISTING routing group separating delivery from the doorbell. Edit class addOnly: 12 added / 0 modified / 0 removed, so the suite self-clears and stays @frozen; no acceptance scenario weakened or deleted. Floor: none. Cold ACED spec-judge over 3 rounds, converging: R1 ALIGNED false (BUILDER — an over-specific Given left the ratified unconditional claim unbound, a `--show`-then-defer config passed the whole suite; ARCHITECT — README restated contracts frozen in the sibling cyberlegion project). R2 ALIGNED false (BUILDER — the same defect had MIGRATED into the When, which named the act under test and handed over the verdict; the register/claim split had also dropped an ordering constraint the conjunction carried silently, since claimPresence throws without a prior register). R3 ALIGNED true, all three lenses, no blocker: both prior escape configs now fail, the conjoined Then judged one act plus its ordering qualifier rather than two separable demands, pairwise consistency clean across the four scenarios sharing `When Operator is seated`. All 12 register a miss against the shipped skill and a config-quoting memorizer. Deferred, not folded in: the pre-existing @rubric scenario (its repair rewrites a frozen scenario and fires Clearance — a different edit class) and the init-cyberlegion hardcoded --handle legate gap, both on the followup record.

note: CORROBORATING EVIDENCE for the @rubric follow-up, from this CR's impl gate: the case-judge scored the conforming implementation 3/3 + 2/2 + 2/2 + 2/2 = 9/9 against threshold 7 — a perfect ceiling on every dimension.
